name: Maypop

facts.what: Egg-sized green fruit; leaves for tea
facts.how: Ripe pulp raw; dried leaves as calming tea
facts.value: Vitamin C; the pulp is fragrant and tart

caution: Eat only the pulp of ripe (yellowed, wrinkling) fruit; green unripe maypops are unpleasant. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: The intricate purple-and-white passionflower is unmistakable; the fruit 'pops' underfoot when ripe, hence the name.

sections.title: Uses
sections.body: Scoop the sweet-tart seedy pulp straight from a ripe fruit. The dried leaves make a traditional mild, calming tea.
